Do not accept 'the units are installed' as evidence that the service works -- re-probe through the socket.

title: [P1] THE OFFLOAD BLOCKER: agents have no build toolchain, so 'the bunker does the building' is not yet true for most projects -- a fresh agent measured go/gcc/make/node/cargo ALL ABSENT, python3 only
source: Workflow proof 2026-09-20 (local git + remote compute, measured)

The loop itself is PROVEN end to end on a fresh agent: code scaffolded through the mount is natively the agent's; a commit made on the control side (f4aa90d) was confirmed as the AGENT's own HEAD, so there is one repository and no sync step; the build ran on the agent and produced its artifact there; with bin/ ignored, git status through the mount stayed CLEAN with the artifact present; and git ls-remote on the control side returned real refs, so the committing side holds the forge credential. ALL OF THAT IS TRANSPORT. THE COMPUTE IS THE GAP: the same probe found go ABSENT, gcc ABSENT, make ABSENT, node ABSENT, cargo ABSENT, with only python3 present. A mount gives a native tree and your credentials; it does not give a compiler. So for any Go/Rust/C/JS project the offload currently does nothing -- the agent cannot build what you want built, however well the mount works. That makes this row the gate on the model being real, not a nice-to-have. Note the division of labour that already exists: tools a DISTRIBUTION ships (compilers, interpreters, language servers) belong to the image-spec package-add path, which pins versions and verifies signatures; only tools we BUILD ourselves are copied (see the agent-tool delivery work). SCOPE: (a) decide and document the toolchain set per agent class, provisioned through the image/provisioning path rather than by copying binaries; (b) make the required set DECLARED and CHECKABLE so a project can ask 'can this agent build me?' and get a named answer instead of a rc=127; (c) prove it by building a real project of a non-Python language entirely on the agent. Reuse the agent-tools dependency-probe shape rather than inventing a second one.

SEPARATE FROM TOOLS-002, which covers ripgrep + a language server for the EDIT verbs; this row is about the BUILD/RUN/TEST toolchains for the compute-offload model, and the two have different owners and different acceptance. Does NOT block the mount workflow, and does not block read-only or interpret-only work. CLOSING CRITERIA: a non-Python project (Go, C or JS) builds and tests ENTIRELY on a fresh agent with no local compute, the required set is declared per agent class and checkable in one command whose absence is NAMED, and the skill guidance matches what is actually provisioned.

title: [P1] PERSISTENT PROJECT DEV BOX: the model wants one KEPT box per project that Hermes reattaches to across sessions, but agents expire by default (6h) and are DESTROYED at expiry, and there is no documented reattach/resume path
source: Bane's dev-box model (2026-09-20): 'connect to the same bunker for a project, things installed cloned managed' + the LAMP/SFTP analogy
reasoning: THE VISION IS A KEPT BOX, AND THE LIFECYCLE IS THE PART THAT IS NOT READY. The intended shape (skill coding-hermes-remote-bunker, 'The Target Shape'): provision the box not the task, one box per project, mounted and driven like a LAMP dev login where things are installed, cloned and managed on the far side. Today, spawning gives a box that is DESTROYED at TTL expiry (manager.go: 'TTL expired, destroying agent'), with a 6h default and heartbeat that never shortens an existing longer expiry. So the pieces exist -- `spawn --ttl 24h`, `heartbeat` to extend, `list` to enumerate -- but nothing states or tests the CONTRACT a kept box actually needs: (a) survive a Hermes/client restart so the loop can reattach to the SAME box with its tree, toolchain and clone intact; (b) a deliberate, visible lifetime rather than an accidental default that kills a box mid-test -- an expiry during a run is indistinguishable from a flaky test; (c) a defined behaviour when a box is NOT extended: what is preserved, what is lost, and whether an unexpired-but-stale box is reclaimable; (d) one-box-per-project enforced or at least conventionalised, so a mount never resolves to another project's tree. WITHOUT THIS, mounting and reattaching is a per-session accident rather than a workflow, and the 'run 30-50 projects at once' economics cannot be relied on -- you cannot keep 30-50 boxes mounted if you cannot guarantee which ones still exist and which tree each owns.
detail: MEASURED today: spawn accepts an explicit --ttl (validated locally before the RPC) and advertises --ttl 24h in its examples; heartbeat extends and explicitly never shortens (6h default unless agent.default_ttl is set; a 7d agent stays 7d); the daemon destroys an agent when its TTL expires; `bunker list` enumerates live agents. What is NOT evidenced: reattaching to a box after the driving client restarts with the mount and workspace intact; a documented lifecycle for a long-lived box (renewal cadence, what a missed renewal does); and any guarantee that per-project boxes cannot be confused. SEPARATE FROM SURF-009 (toolchains on the box) -- this is the box's LIFETIME and IDENTITY, not its contents; both are required for the model and neither substitutes for the other. ALSO RELATED: the doctor habit ('ask the box what it is, every session', bunker agent-tools) is already shipped; the generalization to a declared toolchain set is SURF-009, so do NOT file a second doctor row -- extend that one.
review_notes: PASS: (1) a box spawned with an explicit lifetime is still the SAME box -- same id, same mounted tree, same toolchain, clone intact -- after the driving client or Hermes restarts; (2) the lifetime is visible and renewable, with a documented cadence and a named, non-silent outcome if renewal is missed; (3) expiry during a run cannot be mistaken for a test failure (the failure names the expiry); (4) a mount provably resolves to the intended project's box, and the convention is documented where a user will read it. Do not accept 'spawn with a long TTL' as evidence -- restart the client and prove the box is the same one.

On 2026-09-21 that produced 2 consecutive failures on 22 enabled projects and a mass drop wave at 16:06:53Z (warpfs, duckbrain, coding-hermes-tools, h3-protocol-foreman, 9router-qa, warpfs-sync...), plus a HIGH 'gateway unreachable at startup and exec fallback disabled -- staying idle' at 17:22Z with retries=10. That mode is loud and recoverable -- the gateway unit came back at 17:20Z and the fleet resumed (28 ticks in the 17:00Z hour, 41 in the following 90 min). (2) THE QUIET ONE, AND THE REAL DEFECT: a tick that had already DONE its work and was killed at its final POST leaves work committed but its bookkeeping stranded. bunker-2026-09-21-13-10-19 ran ~2h, landed GAP-117 (code commit 4679c2f, pushed to main) and then died at its gateway POST (15:07Z) -- the board row still read 'pending', the header was a tick behind, and event 702 plus the .gitreins entry sat uncommitted in the working tree. Nothing in the system reports this: the tick row says 'failed', the code says shipped, the board says open, and only a human diffing the tree finds the drift. Worse, the tier-2 verdict written for that tick was FAIL/INCOMPLETE with ZERO criteria items (evaluated_at 15:05:06Z, the minute the tick died) -- so the row was simultaneously work-complete and verdict-failed, and naively trusting either artifact yields a wrong answer. The failure mode generalises: ANY gateway blip during a tick's close-out orphans that tick's closure. Because it is silent, it accumulates -- and it is exactly the class of drift the board exists to prevent. A retry of the close-out, or a re-queue of a tick that died inside its final window, is cheap; a human diffing for stranded closures every time is not.
detail: Reproduce/observe: (a) the drop mode -- `sqlite3 ~/.hermes/coding-hermes/scheduler.db "select name, consecutive_failures from projects where enabled=1 and consecutive_failures>0"` and the events table for component='spawn' with 'gateway unavailable and exec fallback disabled'; (b) the quiet mode -- a tick whose row says failed while `git log` shows its task commit on main and `git status` still shows board files modified. Implemented today was the MANUAL recovery only: the orphaned bookkeeping was landed (9d1570a) and the INCOMPLETE verdict re-fired, because a FAIL-with-0-items is a non-verdict (the evaluator died, it did not evaluate). Do NOT 'fix' this by enabling exec fallback -- --no-exec-fallback is deliberate policy and re-enabling it would trade a visible outage for an invisible one. CLOSING CRITERIA: a gateway outage during a tick's close-out leaves NO stranded closure -- either the close-out is retried until it lands, or the tick is re-queued, or the orphan is detected and reported automatically by name; and a verdict of FAIL with zero criteria items is never recorded as an evaluation (it is INCOMPLETE and must be re-run).
review_notes: PASS: simulate a gateway outage inside a tick's final window and show the closure still lands (or the tick is re-queued with a named event) with no manual diffing; and show that a zero-item FAIL verdict cannot be mistaken for a judged failure. Do not accept 'the gateway recovered' as the fix -- the gateway recovering does not un-orphan the tick that died, and the next blip repeats it.

title: P2 — bunker deploy's internal ssh can fail with 'Too many authentication failures' and leave a PARTIAL tree behind
reasoning: FOUND 2026-09-23 (fleet review programme, subgoal 3) while shipping two exported revisions to a JIT agent. MEASURED: 'bunker deploy /tmp/gr-ab-old <agent>:/home/bunker-<agent>/verify-deploy --server bunker-las-02' printed 'bunker: scp -r: exit status 1' and exited 1, but 49 of 290 source files had already landed in the destination — a partial tree that any consumer ignoring the rc will run against. Root cause, measured: the local ssh-agent holds 7 keys (ssh-add -l) while the target sshd's default MaxAuthTries is 6, so the transfer dies with 'Received disconnect from 100.116.99.35 port 22:2: Too many authentication failures'. The CLI already knows the fix — the ssh lines IT generates for the mount and the docker tunnel both pass '-o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i ~/.bunker/keys/<id>' (visible in spawn output) — but the scp path that 'deploy'/'cp' use does not, so it offers every key on the box. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FAILED COPY: it is silent-at-a-distance. My first A/B attempt consumed the deployment without checking file counts, so both sides ran against directories with no pyproject.toml and reported rc=1 'No module named pytest' in 0s — a green-looking, evidence-free result that a less careful run would have narrated as a test outcome. Same class as DF-GITREINS-POC-25 (failure modes reported as success) and this repo's GAP-143. SUGGESTED FIX: pass -o IdentitiesOnly=yes (and the agent's own key) in the scp used by deploy/cp, and on failure either remove the partial destination or print the landed/total file counts so the partial state is loud. WORKAROUND USED HERE (works, no CLI change): tar the tree, ship one file with an explicit scp '-o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i <agent key>', untar remotely, then ASSERT the file count and the presence of pyproject.toml before running anything — documented in the subgoal-3 artifact. NOTE for whoever picks this up: the same default-identity behaviour applies to 'bunker exec' when the box's ssh-agent is loaded.

title: [P2] the fleet runs three builds of 0.1.4 - local 16fff6d, bunker-mvp a6a52a1, agent host cef10fc (09-12) - and nothing compares a daemon's build to HEAD
reasoning: FOUND 2026-09-23 by the fleet review programme while re-verifying a claim that was TRUE when first measured. THE MATRIX (each host's own version string, which is the evidence): local daemon paths /opt/bunker/bunkerd, ~/go/bin/bunkerd and /usr/local/bin/bunkerd all report 0.1.4 build 16fff6d (09-22) - the repair recorded in GAP-143 holds, the system unit /etc/systemd/system/bunkerd.service is active since 02:28:34, listeners on 127.0.0.1:10001/10002, /healthz 200; the local CLIENT ~/.local/bin/bunker reports 0.1.4 build 00c3555 (09-20) - a different binary from the daemons, not a daemon; the fleet host bunker-mvp 78.46.173.180 reports 0.1.4 build a6a52a1, deployed 2026-09-23T03:55Z by the live lane as part of its own documented E2E step; the AGENT host 100.116.99.35 (/usr/local/bin/bunkerd, per its unit ExecStart) reports 0.1.4 build cef10fc - the 2026-09-12 'chore: release v0.1.4' commit, i.e. THE HOST THAT ACTUALLY RUNS AGENTS IS ON THE OLDEST BUILD IN THE FLEET (11 days behind the local daemon). All four advertise the identical semver 0.1.4, which is exactly why this survived a semver-only check: the earlier evidence for the fleet host read 'Version 0.1.4 ONLINE' with no commit attached. WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN A DRIVE-BY RE-INSTALL: (a) re-installing fixes today and decays again tomorrow, because the install would be a step taken by a review rather than by the lane that commits the code; (b) this is the third instance of one failure shape found in a single day - the gitreins GitLab mirror drifted because a lane's commit sat unpushed ~5.5h (filed REVIEW-GITREINS-017 there) and the dagger binary is 12 commits / 1,647 insertions behind HEAD (filed REVIEW-DAGGER-009 there). The shape: an artifact proves a state was verified ONCE and nothing re-checks it. ASK: build from HEAD with the Makefile (which injects the commit via -ldflags from 'git rev-parse --short HEAD'), install that single build to all three local daemon paths AND the CLI, redeploy the two fleet hosts, then record each host's string in this row - and add a freshness check where the repo already runs its gates, comparing the installed binary's buildinfo (vcs.revision, NOT the printed semver) against git HEAD, failing or warning the tick when the delta touches code paths. TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS recorded so the fix is not built on sand: a bare 'go build' does not inject the commit the way the Makefile does (observed here: a bare build reported 16fff6d while the tree's HEAD was 2b0bd5e), so the printed string is only proof of what runs when the binary came from make; and 'bunkerd --version' vs 'bunker --version' are daemon and client, so comparing them is not a daemon-alignment test. WHY THE ALIGNMENT WAS NOT DONE DURING THE REVIEW: a live bunker tick (status=running, spawned 03:45:31) owns the working tree and its uncommitted edit does not compile at manager_spawn.go:509 (sliceContainmentKnobs now returns two values, caller not updated) - an export of HEAD into a throwaway dir builds CLEAN, so the canon is healthy and no CI or lane is affected; this is a live edit in progress, not a broken repo, and the alignment belongs to that lane. The review deliberately did not touch the tree or file a false 'unbuildable repo' finding.

title: [P1] every `bunker exec` starts a FRESH container - caches, toolchains and apt-installed tools evaporate
reasoning: MEASURED 2026-09-23 on dedi-2 agent km1 (image-spec agent). Two consecutive execs reported different hostnames (9069affcbe23 then 2e70780f8d65); markers written to /tmp and /root in exec 1 were GONE in exec 2; only /home/bunker-km1 survived. Consequences: (a) Go's default caches under /root are lost every call, so a build re-downloads and recompiles from cold unless GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE are exported into the workspace; (b) a backgrounded process dies with its exec, so a build can never be detached and polled; (c) anything installed at runtime (the mf1 foreman hit this: musterflow needs CGO and the image has no C compiler, so every building exec must re-run `apt-get install gcc g++` ~60s). The workspace bind is the ONLY persistence. This is a large, silent performance cliff for remote builds.
detail: Decide and document the model. Either (a) persist per-agent HOME-backed defaults for GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE and any image-spec toolchain so they survive, or (b) make the ephemerality explicit in the docs and provide a canonical 'prepare' step. Also consider keeping the container alive across execs within a session.

title: [P1] git over the sshfs mount, measured: trivial reads cost 10-30s, every whole-tree op stalls, and a stalled cleanup blocks UNKILLABLY in D state
reasoning: MEASURED 2026-09-23 with probes/git-over-mount-probe.sh against a live agent mount (dedi-2, agent mf1, musterflow, only 106 tracked files — so these are NOT large-repo artifacts). Per-op timeout 60s. COMPLETED (5): rev-parse HEAD 10.82s, log -1 22.55s, log --oneline -20 29.54s, ls-files 5.81s, add-one-file 21.26s. STALLED past 60s (9): diff --stat HEAD, status --short, status --porcelain -uno, fetch origin, checkout -b, commit, commit --amend, rebase onto HEAD~1, pull --rebase. The cost is therefore not only in whole-tree reads: checkout, commit and rebase — the primitive WRITE path the remote loop depends on — also fail to complete. The FUSE round-trip dominates every index/object operation. TWO NEW STABILITY HAZARDS fell out of running it, both worse than the timings: (1) THE PROBE'S OWN CLEANUP WEDGED. `git checkout` restoring the base branch entered uninterruptible D state and stayed there; the script had already printed its summary but could not exit, and a D-state process CANNOT be killed (SIGTERM and SIGKILL are both deferred until the I/O returns). Anything driving git over the mount can be stuck permanently with no recourse but waiting. (2) A STALLED COMMIT LEAVES THE INDEX DIRTY. When `git add` succeeds and the following `commit` stalls, the index keeps a staged entry for a file that no longer exists (observed: 'AD .git-mount-probe.txt'). The agent's repo was left non-clean by a probe that only meant to read.
detail: CONCLUSION: the mount is a FILE-EDITING surface, not a git surface. The earlier rule ('read-only git on the agent, writes through the mount') is not strong enough — the writes do not reliably complete either. The honest rule is: treat git as an ON-AGENT operation wherever possible, and reserve the control side for the one step that genuinely needs its credentials: the push. ASKS: (a) update the remote-bunker skill's git guidance to match the measurement; (b) decide whether pushes should move server-side via a credential-forwarding path, which would take the mount out of the git path entirely; (c) give `bunker mount` a bounded-operation guard so a stalled git cannot wedge a driver indefinitely; (d) SURF-014 already says bulk transfer belongs on `bunker cp` — this extends that to the git workflow. UNFINISHED: the probe was cut short after the first repo because the host was saturated (loadavg 58; kswapd0 and jbd2 both in D state; plus the wedged cleanup process). asce1 (1489 files) and km1 (3738 files) were NOT run, so the 106-file number is the FLOOR, not the worst case. Re-run when the box is idle: probes/git-over-mount-probe.sh <mount-repo> --timeout 60

title: [P1] SPIKE: persistent agent container — finish container-mode, or build it on systemd-nspawn / rootless podman instead of docker run --rm
reasoning: DECISION INPUT for Bane, arising from the LXC/LXD evaluation (bunker-specs/bunker-lxc-lxd-evaluation). MEASURED 2026-09-23: image-backed `bunker exec` runs `docker run --rm` PER CALL (internal/server/service.go:1241 containerRunPrefix + :1258 buildAgentImageExecCommand; the --rm is explicit: 'a one-shot exec never leaves a container behind'). Consequences, all observed live on an agent: consecutive execs report DIFFERENT hostnames; /tmp and /root vanish between calls; only the bind-mounted home survives; therefore any runtime install (apt-get install gcc for a CGO build) is paid on EVERY exec (~60s), and Go's caches must be redirected into the home or they re-download each call. `specs/container-mode.md` already designs the fix — a long-lived agent container with the home bind-mounted, persistence matrix and all — but its own status note says it is still design: GAP-064 landed per-agent IMAGE SPECS, not container mode, and SpawnAgentRequest still has no mode field. WHY NOT LXD (so the reasoning is recorded, not just the verdict): LXD/Incus is a PRIVILEGED ROOT DAEMON. The current architecture's deliberate strength is that the host runs NO privileged container daemon — each agent gets its own rootless dockerd as its own unprivileged user via a systemd transient unit. Adopting LXD for the agent surface would regress exactly the axis the containment model optimizes. LXD remains attractive for a DIFFERENT role: an operator-managed, snapshot-heavy build box, not the untrusted-code sandbox. THE SPIKE: before building container-mode on docker, spend one bounded session comparing three ways to get a PERSISTENT, per-agent container that keeps the no-privileged-daemon property: (a) finish container-mode as specced (docker run -d + docker exec), (b) systemd-nspawn (no daemon at all; systemd IS the manager; fits the existing transient-unit habits), (c) a persistent rootless podman container (daemonless AND rootless). Deliverable: a one-page comparison on persistence, uid-mapping correctness for the bind-mounted home, snapshot/clone availability, host privilege introduced, and ops surface — with a recommendation.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: each option demonstrated on dedi-2 with a real repo; for each, prove that an installed tool SURVIVES a second call, that files written in the container are owned 1:1 by the host agent user, and that no privileged host daemon is required. Report the host privilege each option introduces, explicitly. CROSS-REFS: SURF-010 (persistent project dev box), SURF-012 (fresh container per exec), SURF-013 (image lacks python3/rg/cc), specs/container-mode.md section 6 (seven open risks, uid-mapping parity the highest). NOTE: this row is the executable half of a DECISION that stays with Bane — the spike informs it; it does not make it.

title: [P1] bunker env set PATH is silently overridden by exec/run: the SSH session unconditionally sets PATH to ~/bin:/usr/local/sbin:..., ignoring the user-set PATH in /run/bunker/<id>/env

Workaround: use absolute paths or symlink into ~/bin. Fix direction: source the env file AFTER the SSH profile sets PATH, or prepend the user's PATH to the session PATH.

title: [P2] image spec: replace the hardcoded manager switch with a manager registry (ManagerDef)
reasoning: First task of the image-spec expansion wave (Bane 09-23: apt/go/npm 'is a little narrow'). Today adding a manager means editing FOUR places: spec.go (PackageManager const + Valid()), parse.go (validateToken + Dockerfile rendering), proto.go (wire mapping), plus tests. Replace with a registry of ManagerDef{Name, TokenExtra, TokenDeny, Render, Probe} so a new manager is one table row plus tests. BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING: the existing apt/go/npm rendering and every current test must stay byte-identical green. This is the foundation GAP-148..153 all sit on, and GAP-152 (base registry policy) reuses the same registry shape.

Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P1] image spec: quoted-token rendering + per-manager token grammar (the security-critical half)
reasoning: THE blocking piece for every new manager, and security-critical. The token grammar today is `A-Za-z0-9 . + - _ : / @ =` and deliberately excludes every shell metacharacter, because Dockerfile() renders each package into a RUN line that a SHELL then parses. apt/go/npm fit inside it; pip needs `, < > [ ]` (>=2.31,<3 and extras), cargo/gem/composer need `^ ~ > ,`. FIX (structural, not a blacklist): render every package token single-quoted — `RUN pip install --no-cache-dir 'requests>=2.31,<3'` — which makes those characters inert to the shell, and `'` is already forbidden in tokens so the quoting cannot be escaped out of. Then each manager declares ONLY the extra characters its own version grammar needs. Must STAY forbidden for every manager: whitespace, ; & | $ ` \ " ', newlines, and any redirect outside a quoted token.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: per-manager TokenExtra/TokenDeny enforced; every rendered package token is single-quoted; the full injection corpus (curl|sh, semicolon chaining, newline escape, redirection, backticks, $(), quotes, wildcards, unicode) is rejected under EVERY manager, table-driven; and a positive test proves each manager can express its own real version syntax. Existing three managers keep their accepted/rejected sets. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion
guard_result: PASS

title: [P2] image spec: Tier-1 managers — pip, pipx, cargo, gem, composer

title: [P3] image spec: apt_repo — third-party repo + key addition (AWAITING BANE'S CALL: v1 or deferred)
reasoning: The gap the manager list alone does not close: modern toolchains (current Node, some compilers) are NOT in the distro default repos, so a spec needs to add a repository and its key. This is a different SHAPE from a package add and a genuine trust step (it adds a package source the operator did not choose). Flagged in the design as the highest-value / highest-risk v1 candidate, explicitly awaiting Bane's decision on whether it ships in v1 or is deferred. If v1: restrict repo and key to a POLICY ALLOWLIST (operator-set), never a free-form URL, and render the key fetch without any shell chaining.

title: [P2] base-image policy: allowed_registries, optional digest pinning, private-registry credential path
reasoning: Replaces the closed four-image allowlist with a policy-configured REGISTRY allowlist so 'base container from a registry' works: allowed_registries (docker.io/library, ghcr.io/<org>, quay.io), require_digest (pin by sha256 so a moving tag cannot swap the image under a spawn), and a server-side credential path for PRIVATE registries (docker login against the agent's rootless daemon). CRITICAL BOUNDARY: credentials live server-side and are injected, NEVER carried in a spec or returned in a response. Reuses the registry shape from GAP-147.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: policy knobs in ImageSpecConfig with docs; a digest-pinned ref is enforced (tag-only rejected when require_digest); a private-registry pull succeeds end-to-end with credentials never appearing in a spec, a log, or an API response; existing four bases remain allowed by default config. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P3] Tier-B custom Dockerfile support, gated behind allow_custom_dockerfile (off by default)
reasoning: Bane asked for the base container to be able to come 'from docker file or from docker registry'. A Dockerfile is the ONE source that cannot be safe-by-grammar — it runs arbitrary build steps — which is exactly what the current model forbids ('the input is NOT Dockerfile text at all'). So it is Tier B: operator-set, default OFF, with the trust delta documented plainly. This row exists to make the reversal explicit and reviewable rather than a silent policy drift.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: allow_custom_dockerfile=false rejects a Dockerfile carrying spec with a clear error; =true accepts and builds it through the agent's own rootless socket; the config docs state in plain terms that this enables arbitrary build-time execution and is an operator trust decision. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P1] container mode: route the login AND the sshfs mount into the container (docker exec bridge, no in-container sshd)
reasoning: Bane's core container-mode requirement: 'the login ... would route to the container so it never lands on the main namespace of the system'. The spec's exec-parity section frames this and recommends server-side docker exec (good for the API exec path). THE NON-OBVIOUS PART, found while designing: bunker mount is sshfs, i.e. SFTP, SERVED BY THE HOST sshd — so an option that only routes the interactive shell into the container still hands out HOST-namespace file access through the mount (/etc, /run, other agents' homes). RECOMMENDED (iv): keep the host sshd purely as transport and bridge BOTH the login shell and the SFTP subsystem into the container with docker exec — `sshfs -o sftp_server=/usr/bin/docker` -> `docker exec -i --user <uid> bunker-<id> /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server`. Satisfies the constraint for both paths while running NO sshd inside the container (no listening port, no init, no entrypoint surface to police). Requires only openssh-sftp-server in the image.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: with container mode on, an interactive SSH login lands in the container (prove: hostname/OS differs from the host, and /etc of the HOST is not readable); the sshfs mount exposes ONLY the container view (prove a host path outside the home is unreachable through the mount); no sshd is listening inside the container; bunker exec/cp/tunnel client contracts byte-for-byte unchanged. AWAITING BANE'S CONFIRMATION of option (iv) vs (i) sshd-in-container. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P1] container mode: persistent per-agent container (docker run -d) + docker exec exec path, feature-gated
reasoning: The core of container mode, and the fix for today's measured pain: image-backed exec currently runs `docker run --rm` PER CALL (service.go:1241 containerRunPrefix / :1258 buildAgentImageExecCommand, --rm explicit), so consecutive execs get different hostnames, /tmp and /root vanish, and any runtime install is re-paid every call (SURF-012/SURF-013). Container mode spawns ONE long-lived `docker run -d --name bunker-<id>` per agent with the home bind-mounted at the same absolute path, and routes exec to `docker exec`. Reuses the existing bootstrap through waitForDockerd unchanged; spawn/destroy/status transitions stay client-invisible. Feature-gated (agent.container_mode.enabled) so the current path remains the default until proven.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: with the flag on, two consecutive execs hit the SAME container (same hostname, /tmp persists); spawn/list/info/exec/cp/tunnel responses unchanged from the client's view; destroy stops+removes the container BEFORE the daemon stops; with the flag off behaviour is byte-identical to today. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion + specs/container-mode.md

title: [P1] container mode: spec-declared named volumes — reused across recreate, seeded from image, retain-or-prune policy
reasoning: Bane's chosen persistence mechanism, explicitly INSTEAD of LXC/LXD: 'persist ... for non 1-time containers reusing the volumes they have and allowing for volume support is the right set of tasks'. Named volumes are daemon-scoped (no cross-agent visibility, same containment property as the socket), SURVIVE docker rm + recreate (exactly what --rm destroys today), and an EMPTY named volume is seeded from the image content at that path — so a cache volume at /usr/local/go or /root/.cache comes up pre-populated and then persists. Spec shape: "volumes":[{"name":"cargo","path":"/usr/local/cargo"}] with a strict slug name and an absolute, `..`-free path, both builder-rendered. NAMED VOLUMES ONLY, NEVER HOST PATHS — that keeps the bind-mount escape the spec's exclusions section closed firmly shut.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: declared volumes are mounted at docker run and their contents SURVIVE a container recreate; a host-path volume is rejected; a cross-agent volume is unreachable; retain_volumes_on_destroy=false prunes on destroy and =true retains; the seeding property is demonstrated with a real toolchain (e.g. Go cache). Rewrites the spec's persistence matrix. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P2] container mode: restart RPC (container recreate)
reasoning: Container-mode restart maps to container RECREATE (`docker rm -f bunker-<id>` + `docker run -d` with identical image/bind-mount/volume/publish flags), which resets the container layer to image state while host home and volumes persist. The spec records that NO restart RPC exists in bunker.proto or internal/agent today (Constraint B) — so this is net-new proto + handler surface, and it must land WITH GAP-156 so volumes are the documented persistence story rather than an implementation detail. Follows the repo's API conventions: POST-only, connectrpc error codes, snake_case agent_id.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: restart RPC added with proto + handler + CLI; recreate proven to preserve home + volumes and reset the container layer; the client-visible transition matches the existing stopping->running state machine; E2E battery covers it. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P2] container mode: destroy + daemon-restart orphan sweep for container-mode images and volumes
reasoning: Spec section 6 risk 3: no container-mode-aware sweep exists today. Container mode adds two new durable object classes that can outlive their agent — customized IMAGES and named VOLUMES — and the existing daemon-restart orphan handling only stops orphaned containers. Destroy must prune the agent's own volumes/image through the agent's OWN socket (never the host's), in the correct order: container stop+rm, then volume/image prune, then dockerd stop, then userdel. The orphan sweep must clean image/volume leftovers belonging to dead agents.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: destroy leaves no container, image, or volume behind by default (retain flag excepted, and then the retention is explicit and logged); a simulated daemon restart with a dead agent's leftovers results in a clean sweep; only the agent's own socket is ever used. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P1] container mode: uid-mapping parity E2E + full battery VERIFY-PASS on the live server
reasoning: Spec section 6 risk 1 is explicitly the HIGHEST risk: the container runs --user <uid>:<gid> against the host 65536 subuid/subgid mapping, and the home is bind-mounted at the same absolute path — so file ownership between container writes, host, and the sshfs mount must line up 1:1 in both directions. A silent mismatch here would corrupt ownership of a user's real tree, which makes this the gating verification for the whole feature (and it is exactly the class of thing the offload rounds proved matters: verify by destination/content, not by exit code). AGENTS.md is binding on this repo: tasks touching agent spawn/destroy/exec/docker/SSH behaviour REQUIRE the live battery with VERIFY-PASS.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: files created in the container are owned by the host agent uid; files created through the sshfs mount are owned by the container user; round-trip both directions with identity checks; run bash e2e-full-battery.sh against the live server and REQUIRE VERIFY-PASS before the feature is called done. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P2] rewrite the container-mode spec: exclusions, persistence matrix, and a SETTLED exec-parity section
reasoning: The spec currently FORBIDS exactly what Bane is now asking for, so this is a deliberate revision, not an amendment: (a) 'no host bind-mounts beyond the home dir' -> named volumes are now in scope; (b) 'no separate base-image/USER/EXPOSE/VOLUME/ENV policy drift' (VOLUME explicitly excluded) -> volume support is the persistence mechanism; (c) base images never chosen ad hoc from a closed list -> base from registry/Dockerfile under the GAP-152/153 policy. Also: settle the exec-parity section on the confirmed option (iv)/(ii) instead of leaving (i) as an undecided alternative, and update the persistence matrix so volumes read as durable and the writable layer as ephemeral. Specs are the design authority before the wave, so this lands BEFORE implementation completes — AGENTS.md and the repo's docs-vs-reality discipline both point that way.

Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion

title: [P1] adoptAgent re-registers limits from config defaults and NEVER applies the isolation knobs — adopted agents enforce nothing
reasoning: ROOT CAUSE of 'why is the 218% agent not capped'. internal/agent/reconcile.go adoptAgent() (lines 415-451) rebuilds an orphan's tracker record with `Limits: m.defaultLimits()` and then only Register()+persistSpawn(). It never calls applyUserSliceLimits / KnobsForPreset / systemd-run — NOTHING touches the host. So an ADOPTED agent is REPORTED with limits while ZERO of them are applied: the numbers are decoration. Two consequences: (a) a 20 GiB 'disk limit' that does not exist as an enforced bound anywhere; (b) because it re-derives from m.defaultLimits() rather than stored values, the reported limits do not even reflect what the agent was originally spawned with. Cube runs reconciliation.mode: adopt deliberately ('re-registered, not archived and deleted'), so every agent on that box took this path. Evidence, cube-las-00 (100.84.195.43), read-only, 2026-09-23: agent 2cdce4d0 (/var/lib/bunkerd/agents.jsonl) has spawn event limits {disk_max_bytes=21474836480, cpu_quota=4, memory_max_bytes=8589934592}; yet: `systemctl status bunker-docker-2cdce4d0` = 'Unit ... could not be found'; no /etc/systemd/system/user-1003.slice.d/ drop-in; `systemctl show user-1003.slice` reports CPUQuotaPerSecUSec=infinity and MemoryMax=infinity (TasksMax=254284 = system default, not the configured value); /run/bunker/ does not exist; the agent's dockerd runs from a lingering user session (systemd --user PID 2292, up since boot), socket at /run/user/1003/docker.sock. Config on cube sets reconciliation.mode: adopt and does NOT set agent.default_disk_bytes.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: after adopt, the agent's systemd slice/unit carries the same knobs a fresh spawn would apply (verify with `systemctl show user-<uid>.slice -p CPUQuotaPerSecUSec -p MemoryMax -p LimitFSIZE` and by the presence of the per-agent docker unit); a regression test drives adoptAgent with injected runners and asserts the knobs are applied; the reported limits are sourced from the agent's persisted/original values, not from current config defaults. NOTE the design question this exposes: either adopt applies limits, or the CLI must not report limits for adopted agents — silently reporting unenforced limits is the worst of the three.

title: [P1] disk_max_bytes is enforced as LimitFSIZE (a PER-FILE cap) — no mechanism anywhere caps an agent's TOTAL disk
reasoning: The declared 'disk limit' does not mean total disk usage. internal/agent/isolation.go unitKnobsFor() emits `LimitFSIZE=<disk_max_bytes>` for diskMax>0, and internal/agent/run.go:122-123 does the same — LimitFSIZE is RLIMIT_FSIZE, the maximum size of a SINGLE FILE. An agent can therefore sit at 43.6 GB against a '20 GB limit' as long as no individual file exceeds 20 GiB, and nothing else counts bytes. The code comment states this outright: 'pragmatic systemd-level enforcement for disk_max_bytes when per-user filesystem quotas (xfs_quota) are not configured'. Worse, the repo's own internal/agent/SKILL.md directs operators to set default_disk_bytes: 0 because RLIMIT_FSIZE crash-loops .NET apps (Prowlarr/Radarr ftruncate a 2TiB sparse file at first boot -> EFBIG -> SIGXFSZ; 2ed1054) — and the knob is only emitted when >0, so the documented-good configuration is NO disk enforcement at all. Net effect: 'disk_max_bytes' is a REPORTING number, and the CLI's percentage (bunker list -> formatDisk(used, limit) -> '218% (43.6 GB/20.0 GB)') compares real usage against a number no host mechanism enforces. Evidence, cube-las-00 (100.84.195.43), read-only, 2026-09-23: agent 2cdce4d0 (/var/lib/bunkerd/agents.jsonl) has spawn event limits {disk_max_bytes=21474836480, cpu_quota=4, memory_max_bytes=8589934592}; yet: `systemctl status bunker-docker-2cdce4d0` = 'Unit ... could not be found'; no /etc/systemd/system/user-1003.slice.d/ drop-in; `systemctl show user-1003.slice` reports CPUQuotaPerSecUSec=infinity and MemoryMax=infinity (TasksMax=254284 = system default, not the configured value); /run/bunker/ does not exist; the agent's dockerd runs from a lingering user session (systemd --user PID 2292, up since boot), socket at /run/user/1003/docker.sock. Config on cube sets reconciliation.mode: adopt and does NOT set agent.default_disk_bytes.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: either implement genuine total-disk enforcement (see GAP-161) or stop presenting the number as a limit in CLI/API output — one or the other, not both. Add a test pinning the intended semantic so it cannot silently stay 'per-file'. Docs must stop describing default_disk_bytes as a disk cap.

title: [P2] real total-disk enforcement: per-agent filesystem quotas (requires a quota-capable filesystem) or an equivalent
reasoning: The mechanism the code comment names as the real one — per-user filesystem quotas (xfs_quota) — is not available where it is needed. cube-las-00's root is ext4 mounted `rw,relatime,errors=remount-ro` with NO prjquota, so project/user quotas cannot be applied there at all; the same is likely true fleet-wide. Options to evaluate, in rough order of strength: (1) project quotas on a quota-capable filesystem (XFS with pquota, or ext4 with prjquota) mapping each agent's home to a project id — the strongest and the one the comment intends; (2) cap only the container layer store with docker --storage-opt size=<n> (covers the agent's images/layers/volumes but NOT the home — on this box that is 14G of the 42G, so partial); (3) a size-limited backing store per agent (loop/LVM thin volume) — heaviest, most precise; (4) soft enforcement: threshold alerting plus actual reclamation of orphans and caches. Note the interaction with DF-BUNKER-54: LimitFSIZE must NOT be the answer (it breaks sparse-file workloads). Prefer a solution that cannot fail silently into 'unlimited'.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: a decision record comparing (1)-(4) with the per-agent cost and the filesystem prerequisite each imposes; then the chosen mechanism demonstrated on a live agent — attempt to exceed the cap and OBSERVE the refusal at the boundary (bytes, not a percentage), with the agent's other workloads unaffected. Report the filesystem prerequisite explicitly per host.

title: [P2] orphan agent homes are never reclaimed — 40 GB of dead weight on cube; adopt re-registers rather than reaps
reasoning: cube-las-00 carries TWO bunker homes: /home/bunker-2cdce4d0 (42G, user EXISTS, the live agent) and /home/bunker-eduos-agent (40G, NO user, last modified 2026-09-19 14:22). Only one bunker user exists (getent passwd -> bunker-2cdce4d0 only), so the second home is an orphan holding 40 GB that nothing reclaims. Timing suggests a copy left behind rather than a move: the 2cdce4d0 home was created 2026-09-19 14:20:21 and the sibling was modified 14:22:01 — two minutes later — and the two homes have near-identical trees (android-tools 5.2G, models 2.2G, packs 1.2G, wt8 640M, .gradle 503M, go 305M), i.e. one is a duplicate of the other. With reconciliation.mode: adopt, an orphan whose record is missing is RE-REGISTERED rather than removed, so this state can persist indefinitely. title: [P1] container mode: HOME BINDS (class A) — the user's home as the shared storage layer, sources confined to the agent's own home
reasoning: Bane's refinement (09-23): 'the user can keep all that storage on their home directory and mount it to things so they get the feeling like those processes are all writing and reading the same stuff.' Class A = bind mounts whose SOURCE is a subpath of the agent's own home. This is the storage of record and the dev-box feel: several containers on the agent's own dockerd bind-mounting the same home subpath genuinely read one tree, as do `bunker exec` and the sshfs mount — the same bytes everywhere. Lifetime is the home's: it outlives containers, re-spawns and TTL, and it is visible on the host. This row delivers the stated UX requirement, not a convenience. CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FRAMING (recorded because it matters): I first described volumes as reversing the spec's exclusion 'no host bind-mounts beyond the home dir'. That was wrong for class A — the spec ALREADY allows the home as a bind source; it is the one mount it permits. Extending 'the home root' to 'any subpath of the home' preserves the exclusion exactly. Only classes B and C are genuinely new (the spec excludes VOLUME outright). THE BOUNDARY: a bind source must realpath-resolve to a path INSIDE the agent's own home — never /etc, /run, /var, devices, or another agent's tree. Policy: allow_home_binds=true, allow_host_path_binds=false and not configurable on in shipped policy. Spec shape: {"class":"home","sub":"work","path":"/work"}.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: (1) the sharing property — write a file in container A through a home bind, read it from `bunker exec` and from the container B and over the sshfs mount, asserting identical content and ownership; (2) the boundary — a source outside the home is REJECTED, including a `..` traversal AND, critically, a SYMLINK inside the home that points outside it (literal-prefix checking alone passes that; realpath resolution must not); (3) allow_host_path_binds cannot be turned on through the shipped policy. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion (B2).

title: [P2] container mode: EPHEMERAL mounts (class C) — scratch that dies with the container and is shared with nothing
reasoning: Bane's refinement (09-23): 'some just get volumes that get deleted when the container gets deleted — the data doesn't need to be shared.' Class C = the container's own writable layer, or an anonymous volume, for scratch a process needs that nobody should inherit. The point of making it a distinct declared class (rather than 'just don't mount anything') is that the INTENT becomes explicit and testable: a spec says 'this path is scratch', and the platform guarantees it is gone with the container and invisible to siblings. The failure mode to prevent is an ephemeral path silently becoming durable — e.g. landing under a home bind or a named volume by accident — which would leak one container's scratch into another's.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: data written to a class-C path is GONE after the container is removed (and after a recreate); a sibling container cannot see it; and the renderer never emits a persistent mount for a class-C path. Design: bunker-specs/bunker-container-image-expansion (B2).

title: P1 - [Bane 2026-09-23] ROOT CAUSE of the sshfs/git slowness: the agent-host path is a Tailscale DERP RELAY with no port mapping, so every metadata op costs ~142ms and git's whole-tree ops stall. MEASURED on an IDLE box (local loadavg 7.5, swap 5/55G; remote loadavg 6.0) against bunker-las-02: (a) tailscale ping -> 'pong via DERP(lax)' x4 then 'direct connection not established'; (b) tailscale netcheck -> 'PortMapping:' EMPTY (no UPnP/NAT-PMP), nearest DERP is mia at 46.8ms but the relay IN USE is lax at 105.4ms away; (c) RTT to the peer: min 128.6 / avg 179.7 / max 382.2ms with mdev 91.1ms - versus a PUBLIC direct path to Germany at 197.9ms with mdev 0.088ms, i.e. the relayed path is not lower-latency, it is JITTERY, and for a synchronous FUSE filesystem the tail latency is what the user feels; (d) throughput: upload 1.94 MB/s, download 1.77 MB/s on the tailnet versus 4.75 MB/s to Germany over the public internet - a FARTHER destination is 2.4x faster, so the relay caps bandwidth, not distance; (e) sshfs metadata on DISTINCT files: 141.8 ms/op (cache=yes) and 154.1 ms/op (cache=no) - so ~1 op per round trip, as FUSE implies; re-stat'ing the SAME file measures 8.7 ms only because it is cached; (f) sshfs is NOT the bottleneck in isolation: a 10MB write through the mount hit 2.04 MB/s, matching the raw pipe's 1.97 MB/s, and '-o max_conns=8 -o dir_cache=yes' changed nothing (8.6 vs 8.7 ms/op); (g) SSH is NOT misconfigured: negotiated cipher chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com (fast AEAD), compression off (correct default; compression=yes gives 8.67 MB/s on compressible zeros but 1.36 vs 1.72 MB/s on random). CONSEQUENCE, reproducing the 2026-09-23 git-over-mount probe on an idle box with the same ops and 60s timeouts: rev-parse 4.44s, log -1 8.22s, ls-files 1.91s, rev-list 7.88s, cat-file 5.01s, add 12.89s, checkout -b 28.65s - BUT diff --stat, status --short, status --porcelain and commit --allow-empty STILL STALL past 60s. That attributes SURF-018: the stalls are STRUCTURAL (latency x per-file ops), not the local thrash that inflated the original readings ~2.4-5x (rev-parse 10.82s then vs 4.44s now). FIX: obtain a DIRECT tailscale path (enable UPnP/NAT-PMP on the local router, or a static UDP 41641 forward) so the relay hop and its jitter disappear; failing that, note that mia (46.8ms) is 58ms closer than the lax relay actually in use. Also worth a per-peer relay preference check. PASS: 'tailscale ping <host>' reports a DIRECT connection (no DERP hop) and the sshfs metadata op cost on distinct files drops materially from the 142ms baseline (report the new figure); OR, if a direct path is not attainable, a written decision that git stays ON the agent (SURF-018) and only bulk transfer crosses the wire via 'bunker cp'. Measure with the method that works: DISTINCT files, never the same file in a loop (cached reads look 16x faster and hid this for a while).
reasoning: The mount is latency-bound because the path is a DERP relay with 91ms jitter; SSH config is fine.

title: P1 - [Bane 2026-09-23] Every SSH CONNECTION to an agent host costs ~1.6s because there is no connection multiplexing; enabling ControlMaster/ControlPersist cuts it 5.7x. MEASURED against bunker-las-02: one connect+exec round trip = 1634 ms (dedi-2: 2591 ms); 50 ops as 50 SEPARATE connections = 1849.5 ms/op, while 50 ops INSIDE one connection = 47 ms/op - i.e. the cost is entirely per-connection handshake, not per-operation. A 5-connection test: CURRENT 1589 ms/conn; GSSAPIAuthentication=no only 1548 ms/conn (so GSSAPI is NOT the cause); ControlMaster=auto+ControlPersist 278 ms/conn; both 290 ms/conn. Realistic burst of 20 connections: 31.6 s CURRENT vs 5.5 s MULTIPLEXED. Root cause is config, not auth: 'ssh -G' shows controlmaster false / controlpersist no (no multiplexing) while auth is already tight - 2 key attempts per host with IdentitiesOnly yes and an explicit IdentityFile, so key-scanning is NOT the problem either. This is SEPARATE from MOUNT-011: the path (DERP relay, 128-382ms RTT, mdev 91ms) sets the 142 ms/op cost WITHIN a mounted connection, whereas this row is about paying a full handshake per NEW connection - which is what every bunker exec / cp / ssh-driven CLI call does. FIX: add ControlMaster=auto, ControlPath and ControlPersist to the ssh config for the bunker hosts (client-side, no server change, no product change). PASS: a 5-connection burst measures materially below the 1589 ms/conn baseline with the master warm (prove it with the same 5x and 20x burst method used here); 'ssh -O check' confirms the master is in use; the bunker CLI's ssh-driven operations get faster with no behavioural change. NOTE: verify that whatever wraps these connections (bunker exec, sshfs) tolerates a shared master - sshfs mounts its own long-lived connection and must not be multiplexed onto an unrelated master, so scope the ControlPath per host and test the mount after the change.
reasoning: 1.6s per SSH connection is handshake cost; multiplexing proven 5.7x faster; GSSAPI irrelevant.

title: P1 - [Bane 2026-09-24] PROVEN single-variable: git over sshfs fails on LATENCY, not bandwidth and not sshfs. CONTROL EXPERIMENT, same repo (150 files), same sshfs, same mount options, same 8 git ops, same 60s timeout, measured back-to-back on an IDLE control host (loadavg 3.5-7.5, swap 5/55G) - only the DISTANCE changed: SHORT = N100 backup host, direct LAN peer 192.168.123.140:41641, RTT 4.45/41.2/78.0ms (mdev 26.8), upload 3.15 / download 3.78 MB/s, metadata 20.3 ms/op; LONG = Hetzner dedi-2 (Germany, public), RTT 197.79/197.88/198.04ms (mdev 0.088), upload 3.18 / download 3.23 MB/s, metadata 292.2 ms/op. BANDWIDTH DIFFERS BY ~1% (and download is BETTER long-range) while git differs 20-47x: rev-parse 0.22s vs 6.84s (31x), log -1 0.42s vs 13.35s (32x), ls-files 0.13s vs 3.60s (28x), add one file 0.40s vs 18.74s (47x), checkout -b 2.13s vs 43.74s (21x), and THE THREE THAT STALL LONG-RANGE ALL COMPLETE SHORT-RANGE: status --short 5.18s vs STALL>60s, diff --stat HEAD 1.17s vs STALL>60s, commit --allow-empty 2.61s vs STALL>60s. THIRD DATA POINT (bunker-las-02, Tailscale DERP-relayed via lax): RTT 129.96/165.09/266.37 (mdev 46.4), 1.94/1.77 MB/s, metadata 141.8 ms/op - its AVERAGE RTT is LOWER than Hetzner's yet it performs WORSE, because its jitter is 46ms: a synchronous filesystem pays the TAIL, not the average, which is why a rock-steady 198ms public path beats a jittery 165ms relayed one. MECHANISM: sshfs is FUSE-over-SFTP, so every stat/open/readdir/close is a SYNCHRONOUS round trip; the cost of an op is latency and the cost of a workflow is latency x operation count. Hence the failure clustering: rev-parse/ls-files/cat-file touch a handful of files (seconds even long-range); status/diff --stat lstat EVERY file (150 x per-op cost = >21s of stats alone, past 60s); commit is a CHAIN (index lock, object write + fsync, ref update + rename, directory fsync) so it stalls even --allow-empty. FIX: a DIRECT path with low jitter (no relay hop) - the N100 column is the existence proof that a low-latency path makes the ENTIRE git workflow work. Bandwidth is NOT the lever: three ends all measured ~2-4 MB/s while git spread 47x, and neither the local NIC (1000 Mb/s) nor parallel streams (7.53 MB/s to Germany) is saturated. PASS: re-run /tmp/sshfs-full-report.sh against the fixed path and show the metadata ms/op and the stall set both improve from THIS baseline; a path whose jitter is high will keep stalling even at a good average RTT, so require low mdev, not just low average.
reasoning: Single-variable proof: same bandwidth, 14x latency, 20-47x git cost; the long-range stalls all complete short-range. It is distance, not sshfs and not bandwidth.

title: P2 - [Bane 2026-09-24] EVALUATE rclone mount (SFTP backend, request pipelining) as the mounted-workflow transport at distance, because sshfs's slowness is an UPSTREAM ARCHITECTURAL LIMIT with no config fix. EVIDENCE THAT IT IS NOT OUR CONFIG: libfuse/sshfs issue #300 (OPEN, 20 thumbs) is titled 'sshfs is much slower than rclone mount over high-latency connections due to lack of SFTP pipelining' and states a 200ms connection yields 1 MB/s where TCP does 100 MB/s. Mechanism, in upstream's words: OpenSSH caps packets at 256 KiB, which 'effectively disables TCP Window Scaling', and although SFTP allows 'multiple requests may be pending simultaneously' (pipelining), 'sshfs does not seem to implement request pipelining, thus it is much slower' - whereas 'rclone implements pipelining with its SFTP concurrency setting, defaulting to 64'. WE ELIMINATED OUR STACK: client local pipe 2448 MB/s; 'ssh localhost' full crypto path 196.5 MB/s (so not cipher/client); cgroup cpu.max = max 100000 (unlimited); remote CPU ~17% busy/80% idle during transfer; remote sshd has no UseDNS and no GSSAPI (clean); sshfs is 3.7.6 (newest, FUSE lib 3.18.2). WE TRIED EVERY SUPPORTED OPTION against the failing case (Hetzner 198ms, 110-file repo, 30s timeout): default metadata 225.4 ms/op with status and commit STALLED; kernel_cache 215.9 ms/op, add 11.03s->5.42s, but status/commit STILL STALL; compression=yes 227.7 ms/op, still stalls; max_conns=8 226.4 ms/op and rev-parse WORSE (9.62s vs 6.81s) because git is a SERIAL workload and parallel connections cannot overlap sequential requests; and the two options with real theoretical leverage - writeback_cache and sshfs_sync=no - are REJECTED by the build as 'unknown option'. So nothing is left to configure. SECOND CAUSE FOUND (bufferbloat): the short LAN path measures 5.8/7.9/14.2 ms idle but 27.3/55.1/78.0 ms UNDER LOAD, and 256KiB/55ms = 4.8 MB/s against our measured 3.2-3.8 MB/s - which is why even a same-subnet path never behaved like a 2ms path. FIX: benchmark rclone mount over the same SFTP transport and the same git battery. Reports elsewhere show ~4x (rclone community, attributed to multiple TCP connections) and one same-host comparison at 120+ MB/s where sshfs managed a fraction. PASS: mount the SAME 110-file repo via rclone mount against the SAME host, run the SAME eight-op battery with the SAME timeouts, and report the delta in metadata ms/op and in the stall set against the sshfs baseline recorded here; include the mount invocation and rclone's --sftp-concurrency value. If it clears the stalls, it becomes the documented transport for a mounted workflow at distance; if it does not, record that and close the mounted-workflow line. ALSO consider the bufferbloat fix independently (SQM/QoS on the local router, or wired instead of WiFi) since it lifts the bulk ceiling on every path including bunker cp.
reasoning: sshfs's git failure is an upstream architectural limit (no SFTP pipelining, issue #300); no option fixes it; rclone mount is the pipelining alternative the issue itself names.

title: P2 - [Bane 2026-09-24] EVALUATE Mutagen as the remote-dev file strategy: SYNCHRONISE instead of mounting, so git runs against local disk at full speed and the latency class disappears entirely. WHY THIS IS THE STRATEGIC PICK: the sshfs failure is not a tuning problem (see MOUNT-011/013) - git dies because it issues thousands of SEQUENTIAL metadata round trips, and no mount-level option fixes that (writeback_cache and sshfs_sync=no are rejected by our build; max_conns made rev-parse WORSE because a serial workload cannot use parallel connections). Mutagen changes the strategy: it keeps a real LOCAL copy of the tree and propagates changes with a differential algorithm plus low-latency filesystem watching, so the editor, grep and GIT all operate on local disk. It is also what Docker Desktop itself uses for file sharing (Mutagen is joining Docker). INSTALL EFFORT - the criterion Bane set: single binary, Linux/macOS/Windows, NO FUSE, no kernel module, NO ROOT; 'mutagen sync create ./repo user@host:/path/repo'. That is strictly easier than every mounted option (rclone needs macFUSE on macOS and WinFsp on Windows; NFS needs nfsd plus root both ends and Services-for-NFS on Windows). Survey of the full landscape is at bunker-specs/bunker-remote-fs-options. RISKS TO TEST EXPLICITLY: bidirectional sync propagates DELETES both ways, so the sync scope must be deliberate; .git must be handled consciously (sync it so the remote can commit, or ignore it and run git on one side only); symlinks and large node_modules trees need ignore rules; and first-sync cost on a big tree needs measuring.
reasoning: Sync beats a mount over high latency: git gets local disk, so the sequential-round-trip failure class vanishes. Easiest install story of any option - single binary, no FUSE, no root.

title: [P1] bunker spawn cannot fetch the agent SSH key on an auth-enforced daemon - every spawn prints 'could not fetch SSH key: unauthenticated: missing Authorization header' and no key is saved locally
detail: REPRO 2026-09-25 on bunker-mvp (daemon 0.1.4 f525639, auth enforced): `bunker spawn --server bunker-mvp --ttl 10m x` creates the agent but warns 'unauthenticated: missing Authorization header' and writes NO ~/.bunker/keys/<id>. Standalone repro (go run, real daemon): SpawnAgent WITH header 200; GetAgentKey WITHOUT header -> 'unauthenticated: missing Authorization header'; GetAgentKey WITH header -> 200 + 411-byte key. Raw REST with the same token gets 200 on GetAgentKey, so the daemon is fine; the bug is client-side. v0.1.3 binary does not call GetAgentKey (no warn, but also no key), so this regressed with GAP-128. title: [P0] spawn can hand out a numeric uid a host-docker container already runs as; destroy then refuses forever and the TTL reaper retries unbounded (--force does not bypass)
detail: REPRO 2026-09-25 (dogfood run 19, scratch HEAD daemon on a host that also runs host-docker containers): agent fad4b89a spawned as uid 1001 - the same uid an UNRELATED production container (imhotep-backend-1, started Sep 23 by the PREVIOUS agent that held uid 1001, orphaned when that agent was destroyed) still runs as. Measured: from inside the agent, `kill -0 7085` SUCCEEDS (same-uid signal privilege over the production container process) and /proc/7085/cmdline is readable - the isolation promise (isolated Linux user) is broken whenever spawn reuses a uid that a surviving container process holds. Destroy correctly refuses (manager gate: 'user ... still owns live processes that userdel -rf would orphan' with exact pid/evidence - the gate itself is RIGHT); but (a) spawn does not CHECK for this collision up front, (b) the TTL reaper then loops forever: expired -> destroy refused -> repeat every minute, agent stuck 'running' in list/registry indefinitely, and (c) `bunker destroy --force` ('Force destroy even if agent is running') does NOT bypass the gate - there is no operator exit hatch. Host observed: containers under numeric uids in the 1000+ range are common (dexdat stack, imhotep, heading).
reasoning: Breaks BOTH core promises at once (isolation + lifecycle) on any host where docker containers outlive their agents; the reaper loop also means the residue counter grows forever and the agent can never be re-spawned under the same id.
fix_direction: 1) spawn: pre-check candidate uid against live host processes (same probe the destroy gate uses) and pick a uid no live process owns; 2) destroy: document --force semantics or add a real bypass (--force --release-uid) that destroys the bunker record WITHOUT userdel when the blocking processes are not the agent's (compare process start time vs agent creation time - a process older than the agent is by definition not the agent's); 3) reaper: cap retries + loud residue escalation instead of infinite retry. PASS: spawn never allocates a uid held by a live process; an agent wedged by a foreign same-uid process can be destroyed with --force (record removed, user kept, residue reported).

title: [P2] TLS refusal UX: status exits 0 on pin-mismatch/expired/contradictory refusals (list exits 1); TOFU banner claims pin stored when auth failed and nothing was stored; config refusal surfaces as 'stream error: unavailable:'; http-vs-TLS says 'internal: 400 Bad Request'
detail: REPRO 2026-09-25 (dogfood run 19, nine-arm TLS battery, scratch HEAD daemon a4e98ce): (a) with a deliberately re-keyed daemon, `bunker status` prints the full loud pin-mismatch refusal (correct message, both fingerprints, re-pin command) but exits 0 - while `bunker list` exits 1 on the same state; a scripted `bunker status || alert` gate never fires on a MITM-looking condition. Same exit-0 on the contradictory-tls refusal (pinned entry + tls_insecure: true) and on the expired-cert state. (b) Fresh-home `connect --tls self-signed ... --token WRONG`: TOFU banner prints 'stored as cert_pin in ~/.bunker/config.yaml' but NOTHING is stored (verified: empty BUNKER_HOME stays empty, real config untouched) - the banner also hardcodes the default path even when BUNKER_HOME relocates it. (c) After an ack'd insecure connect, the next invocation's insecure-dial refusal (correct per-invocation ack rule) arrives as 'stream error: unavailable: refusing to dial ...' - a deliberate local config refusal dressed as a transport error (wrong error class). (d) `connect http://127.0.0.1:18093` against the TLS listener refuses (good) with 'internal: 400 Bad Request' - could name the scheme mismatch.
reasoning: Messages are excellent; the exit codes and error classes under script control are the weak edge - a security refusal that exits 0 is a monitoring hole.
fix_direction: 1) status (and any reporter command) exits 1 when the underlying RPC was REFUSED (pin mismatch/expired/contradiction) vs merely unreachable - or at minimum a dedicated --fail-on-refusal flag; 2) TOFU banner: only claim persistence after the entry write succeeds, and echo the ACTUAL config path (BUNKER_HOME-aware); 3) classify local config refusals as FailedPrecondition/InvalidArgument (not Unavailable) so clients can distinguish; 4) scheme-mismatch message. PASS: status exits non-zero on pin-mismatch; banner text matches reality under BUNKER_HOME.

title: [P1] renew never re-fetches the agent SSH key - after every successful renewal ssh/cp/mount are dead while RPC verbs still work
detail: Live-proven 2026-09-25 (dogfood run 20, fleet daemon 6a6ad20 + HEAD daemon a4e98ce): renew re-spawns the agent, the daemon persists a NEW keypair (internal/agent/manager_spawn.go:822), spawn fetches it via GetAgentKey (internal/cli/spawn.go:228) - but internal/cli/renew.go never calls GetAgentKey, so ~/.bunker/keys/<id> keeps the OLD key (mtime unchanged through the renew). Observed after renew: bunker cp exit 255 (scp Permission denied), bunker mount preflight Permission denied, direct ssh denied; bunker exec (token RPC) still fine. Fix direction: after the re-spawn leg, make renew run the same GetAgentKey fetch+save spawn does (and overwrite the local key file atomically). Recovery for users on daemons >= 325da4c: POST /bunker.v1.Bunkerd/GetAgentKey {"agent_id":...} with master token, write sshPrivateKey to ~/.bunker/keys/<id>, chmod 600. On the deployed 0.1.4 fleet daemon the RPC does not exist - no recovery path.
fix_direction: renew.go: after re-spawn success, fetch GetAgentKey with the same auth'd client and save to ~/.bunker/keys/<id>; fail loud if the fetch fails (the agent is then ssh-unreachable).
reasoning: code-anchored: spawn.go:228 vs renew.go; live repro on two daemon versions

title: [P1] destroy live-process gate: remedy unsatisfiable agent-side (rootless-docker session services respawn) and gate ABSENT on the deployed 0.1.4 fleet daemon (renew destroys live agents)
detail: Two halves, both live-proven 2026-09-25 (run 20). (a) HEAD daemon: the gate fires correctly (names uid + pids) but the counted processes are the rootless-docker login session's OWN services (dbus-daemon, pipewire, wireplumber, mpris-proxy under the agent uid). The documented remedy (docs/renewal.md: stop those processes, then retry) is unsatisfiable from inside the agent: bunker exec reaps children at session close; run --detach systemctl --user stop does not stick; pkill -u <uid> gets respawned by the user systemd default.target. Only host-root can clear them, so renewing ANY agent that ever ran rootless-docker requires a host maintenance window. (b) deployed fleet daemon 0.1.4 @ 6a6ad20 (pre-gate, 385 commits behind HEAD): renew succeeded exit-0 while the uid owned live processes (rootless dockerd, sd-pam, slirp4netns, a held exec session) - the orphan scenario the gate exists to prevent. Fix direction: (a) exclude the agent-session service set (or stop-and-wait them daemon-side inside destroy with a bounded grace), (b) note in renew docs that daemons < destroy-gate must not be renewed; CLI could refuse on daemon version.
fix_direction: daemon: destroy should treat the rootless-session service set as stoppable by the daemon itself (bounded systemctl --user stop + wait) instead of demanding the operator do it agent-side; CLI: probe daemon version and warn/refuse renew when the gate is absent.
reasoning: gate semantics + rootless session lifecycle; two daemon versions tested

title: [P1] containment landing gate fails standard/hardened spawns on bunker-las-03: systemd needs ~125-349ms to land MemorySwapMax=0, the code allows 125ms (5 reads x 25ms)
detail: Live-proven 2026-09-25 (run 20): every standard-preset spawn on bunker-las-03 fails 'spawn ... failed at stage slice-limits: containment landing did not converge within 5 reads: memory.swap.max = "max", want "0" (bar swap)' with full user rollback (3/3 attempts; fleet daemon unaffected - it predates the gate; run 19 on the SAME box/binary succeeded this morning, so this is timing headroom, not config). Fix direction: raise the convergence budget (e.g. 40 reads x 50ms = 2s) or read the drop-in consumed state via systemctl show instead of raw cgroup files, and add --preset passthrough to renew.

title: P2 - [Bane 2026-09-24] PATCH EXPERIMENT: implement readdirplus in sshfs. WHY IT IS SMALL: the attributes are ALREADY on the wire and ALREADY parsed - struct dir_entry carries 'struct stat stbuf' (sshfs.c:231-234) and sshfs_readdir ALREADY passes them to FUSE ('filler(dbuf, entry->name, &entry->stbuf, 0, 0)' at sshfs.c:2546). CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER READING: I first inferred from the ops table that sshfs discards dir attrs; that was wrong, the data is handed over - what is missing is the FLAG. THREE SMALL THINGS ARE ACTUALLY MISSING: (1) .readdirplus is NOT registered in fuse_operations (sshfs.c:3804+ has .readdir only) - and libfuse docs say the feature 'is enabled by default when supported by the kernel and if the filesystem implements a readdirplus() handler'; (2) the filler is called with flags 0, not FUSE_FILL_DIR_PLUS, so the kernel ignores the attrs being passed; (3) sshfs_init never requests FUSE_CAP_READDIRPLUS (it handles FUSE_CAP_ASYNC_READ and sets FUSE_CAP_EXPORT_SUPPORT only). So the work is roughly: implement sshfs_readdirplus sharing the existing enumeration with FUSE_FILL_DIR_PLUS, register it, request the capability (optionally READDIRPLUS_AUTO), and handle one documented correctness caveat - tens of lines in one file, NOT a rewrite of the request model. THE CAVEAT IS NAMED IN THE SOURCE ITSELF (sshfs.c:196-206): 'SSHFS currently does not return attribute information for readdir() ... Should SSHFS implement a readdirplus() handler ... this is a problem that will need to be solved' - namely a PENDING WRITE can change a file's length so listing attrs can be stale. Bounded: detect in-flight writes in the directory and fall back to a real getattr for those, or do not trust the size field for them. WHY IT MATTERS: git status / git diff --stat / rsync scans issue a getattr per file - one round trip EACH today. With readdirplus the kernel gets names AND attrs per directory in one call. On the 150-file fixture at ~292 ms/op that is ~150 round trips (~44s, past the 60s timeout in practice) versus ~6 (~1.8s). Our build is sshfs-3.7.6-12-ga5d0c9b, only 12 commits behind upstream HEAD.
reasoning: The highest-leverage fix found so far: patch sshfs to implement readdirplus, which collapses whole-tree git ops from one round trip per FILE to one per DIRECTORY. The patch surface was read out of the real source (cloned, 4,737 lines, one core file sshfs.c) - see bunker-specs/bunker-remote-fs-test-plan section 8.
detail: ACCEPTANCE: (D1) a patched build with readdirplus implemented and registered; (D2) Fixture A battery re-run on the same paths with the whole-tree ops completing where they previously stalled, reporting the delta; (D3) CORRECTNESS: 'git status --porcelain' output byte-for-byte identical to unpatched on a tree with known modified/untracked/deleted files, and attribute freshness checked after a write (the staleness caveat); (D4) the diff size reported so 'keep the patch' is a costed decision. Test plan: bunker-specs/bunker-remote-fs-test-plan section 6 and 8.

title: [P1] rootless dockerd fails to start on spawned agent when the daemon recycles a uid whose RootlessKit state dir survived: agent reports 'running' with docker dead (stale /run/user/<uid> lock from a same-day destroyed agent)
detail: Dogfood run 21, 2026-09-25, live bunker-mvp. Evidence: agent dfops0925c (HEAD CLI spawn, healthy SSH surface) -> `docker --version` fine but `docker ps` inside agent = 'dial unix /run/bunker/dfops0925c/docker.sock: connect: no such file or directory'; systemctl --user docker.service = failed, journal: "[rootlesskit:parent] error: failed to lock /run/user/1007/dockerd-rootless/lock, another RootlessKit is running with the same state directory?" repeated at restart counter 3. Server-side: uid 1007 was previously owned by bunker-conctest-3-91761 (snoopy log 2026-09-25 04:24:13, same uid, dockerd-rootless.sh exec) whose user was destroyed; /run/user/1007 persisted (root-owned dirs) and dockerd-rootless/lock with it. `bunker info` shows Status: running the whole time - no health signal. A manual `systemctl --user start docker.service` inside the agent SUCCEEDED once the stale dir was cleared (journal shows clean startup 19:13:43), so the failure is only the stale state dir. Second spawn on the next fresh uid (dfops0925d) started docker fine - confirms per-uid state-dir hygiene as the variable. FIX DIRECTION (a) spawn: after userdel, scrub the uid's /run/user/<uid> rootless state dirs (or refuse to recycle a uid with a live /run/user entry); (b) detectability: bunker info / agent status should reflect docker.service liveness (it already tracks the socket path - report it as degraded instead of running) so users do not debug sshfs/tunnel first.

Evidence: on keyless agents (DF-BUNKER-71 state), `bunker cp /tmp/dfops-file.txt dfops0925:/tmp/dfops-file.txt --server bunker-mvp` -> 'SSH key not found at "/home/kara/.bunker/keys/dfops0925" - spawn the agent first or use --ssh-key'; `bunker ssh` same. A user who loses ~/.bunker/keys/<id> (fresh laptop, wiped config) has NO command to recover: not `key` (that is API-key management), not `agent-tools`, not `info`. FIX DIRECTION: `bunker key fetch --agent <id>` (or reuse the existing GetAgentKey wire) writing ~/.bunker/keys/<id>; alternatively have cp/ssh/mount offer the fetch in their error message ('key missing; run bunker key fetch --agent <id>'). Small, high-value, self-service recovery.
reasoning: Hit while trying the documented cp workflow on a keyless agent; the error text is honest but a dead end - 'spawn the agent first' is wrong for an already-running agent, and the key is sitting server-side one RPC away.

title: [P2] audit list is O(file): 60k-line log takes 209-259ms even with --limit 20 (limit applied only after a full-file scan+parse)
reasoning: Perf lane 2026-09-26-01-53-25, measured on karaHermes (release binary bunker 0.1.4 a4e98ce). `bunker audit list --limit 20` must still scan, JSON-parse and match every record in the audit log: internal/audit/query.go queryFile() reads all lines with bufio.Scanner and json.Unmarshal's each, then Query() (query.go:44-50) truncates records to f.Limit only AFTER the whole file is loaded. Input-scale probe (hyperfine, warmup 2, runs 15, -N): limit-20 @ 6k lines = 25.3 ± 1.4ms; limit-20 @ 60k lines = 214.8 ± 11.7ms (8.5x time for 10x lines — linear in file size, i.e. --limit does not bound the work). Full-list @ 60k = 252.1 ± 6.9ms. Profile evidence (samply record --save-only, 420ms total weight across 20 bunker threads, leaf-frame resolution via addr2line/nm against /tmp/bunker-prof): encoding/json leaf frames total ~38% (checkValid 6.7%, unquoteBytes 3.7%, literalStore 3.0%, state machine frames ~8%, rescanLiteral ~4%), runtime.memmove 5.2% (scanner copies + unmarshal allocations); futex 35.7% is multithreaded-runtime idle, not the parse itself. Expected win (NOT yet verified — this is the implementation): for --limit N with no --since/--until, read the file BACKWARD and stop after N matched records; a 60k-line query for the last 20 records should drop from ~209ms to ~1-2ms (parse only ~20-100 lines) — same shape as `tail -n`, no change to output order or semantics. Also usable: skip match() work for records already outside the time window before json.Unmarshal via a cheap substring pre-filter — smaller win, more risk of false skips. Files: internal/audit/query.go (queryFile loop, lines ~86-108; Query limit truncation, lines ~44-50). Repro: hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 15 -N 'bunker audit list --path /tmp/audit-perf-60k.log --limit 20' with the 60k synthetic log described in the row evidence (generated by replaying 60k mutated copies of the real /var/log/bunkerd/audit.log records).

evidence.command: hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 15 -N -n 'limit-20 @ 6k lines' 'bunker audit list --path /tmp/audit-perf-6k.log --limit 20' -n 'limit-20 @ 60k lines' 'bunker audit list --path /tmp/audit-perf-60k.log --limit 20'

title: [P0] image-spec package-add agents are UNUSABLE as agents: spawn builds a fresh container image and exec/ssh never reach the agent userland — no docker binary in PATH, no /run/bunker/<id>/env file (env set fails), exec runs as ROOT not the agent user, agent-tools probe reports git ABSENT on an agent whose exec works

(b) exec inside the container reports `whoami`=root, uid=0 — the stock agent runs as the agent user. (c) `docker info` inside = 'docker: not found' — the container image (ubuntu:24.04 + 3 apt packages) has no docker CLI and no docker socket bind-mounted into it, so rootless docker is unreachable from exec. (d) agent-tools probe on dfspec-e: git ABSENT+REQUIRED (git exists on the stock agent) — the probe itself runs through the same container path, so its view of the agent is the container, not the agent. (e) `bunker exec --raw -- docker info` execs the host agent userland but PATH lacks $HOME/bin resolution for docker (docker lives at $HOME/bin/docker — raw mode execs 'docker' from PATH and fails). The GAP-064 image-spec promise (spawn --image-spec customizes the agent image) delivers an image whose exec surface CANNOT do the two things agents exist for: docker workflows and env-configured commands. The stock-image agent (dfspec-a) in the same window: exec ok, env ok, git present, docker works, agent-tools REQUIRED git present. FIX DIRECTION: image-backed exec must bind-mount the agent's own /run/bunker/<id>/ (docker.sock + env) into the container and run as the agent uid (--user $(id -u)), or fall back to host-context exec with the agent PATH when the command targets docker/env; alternatively image-spec exec should require the image to derive FROM the stock agent base (not bare ubuntu). PASS: on an image-spec agent `bunker env set` succeeds, `bunker exec -- docker info` reports rootless 29.x, agent-tools probe sees the real agent userland (git present), and exec runs as the agent user.

title: [P0] root-suite CI quarantine raced a production spawn and destroyed a LIVE agent mid-window: user+home+keys swept at 01:53:05 while the daemon registered the agent 'running' at 01:53:04 — heartbeat, exec-RPC and TTL reaping all keep serving a corpse; reconciliation never repairs it
reasoning: REPRO 2026-09-26 (dogfood run 22, bunker-mvp = CI runner): dfspec-d spawned with --image-spec at 01:53:04 (daemon log 'agent spawned successfully', key persisted /etc/bunkerd/ssh/dfspec-d at 01:52:13). ONE SECOND LATER (01:53:05) the repo's own CI root-suite cleanup (snoopy: cwd=/opt/actions-runner/_work/bunker/bunker, mv /etc/bunkerd/ssh/dfspec-d + .pub to /tmp/root-suite-quarantine-khpjJ7/, then userdel -rf) removed the agent: user GONE, home GONE, server key GONE — while bunker list reports the agent 'running', heartbeat ACKNOWLEDGES and extends TTL to 07:57:44, and the CLI happily saved the client key. INT-SPAWN-006's refresh narrows but does not close it. FIX DIRECTION: (1) the sweep must consult the daemon's registry AT SWEEP TIME for each candidate (per-key GetAgent-style check, not a pre-collected ID list); (2) the daemon must reconcile host-truth against its registry on a TIMER (user missing -> mark destroyed/failed, never serve heartbeat for a corpse); (3) root-suite should refuse to run (or use coexist ports + an isolated bunkerd) when a production daemon shares the host. PASS: an agent spawned during a CI suite window survives the suite (list/heartbeat/exec all correct afterwards); a force-deleted agent user is reconciled to destroyed within one tick with a loud residue log.
